Justyna Gudzowska: Justyna Gudzowska has spent her career at the intersection of illicit finance and international security.  She is an expert on sanctions, corruption, terrorism financing, and money laundering, having worked on these issues across the public and private sectors. She is currently the Executive Director of The Sentry, an investigative and policy organization that seeks to expose and disrupt actors profiting from the conflict, corruption, and natural resource exploitation that drive human suffering. She is also an Adjunct Professor at Georgetown University's School of Foreign Service (SFS) where she teaches a class on illicit finance, and an Associate Fellow at the UK-based Royal United Services Institute (RUSI). She has taught at Yale Law School as a Visiting Lecturer in Law. Prior to joining The Sentry, Justyna was the lead sanctions attorney at Morgan Stanley, a counter-terrorism financing expert at the UN Security Council, and a sanctions attorney at the US Department of the Treasury.
Katherine Wilkins: Dr. Katherine Wilkins is an anti-corruption and governance specialist with more than 15 years of experience. As Policy and Advocacy Coordinator at Transparency International, she covers global corrupt money flows. Previously, Wilkins was Specialist for Anti-Corruption and Civic Engagement at Open Society Foundations. Katherine holds a Ph.D. in Political Science from the Hertie School of Governance in Berlin, Germany, an M.P.A. in International Policy and Management, and a B.A. in Russian and Slavic Studies, both from New York University.
Katja Bechtel: Global expert in business integrity and governance with 15+ years at WEF and TI, driving ethical leadership.
Ketakandriana Rafitoson: Ketakandriana “Ke” Rafitoson is a Political scientist and a Human Rights Defender from Madagascar. She is serving as Transparency International Madagascar’s Executive Director since 2018 and has been elected as Transparency International’s Vice-Chair in November 2023. Ke holds a PhD in Political science from IEP Madagascar and a PhD in Social sciences applied to Development from the Catholic University of Madagascar, where she is also lecturing. She is a member of the International Board of the Fisheries Transparency Initiative (FiTI), and of the African Women Against Corruption Network (AWACN)’s Advisory Board, and is also serving as the volunteer National Coordinator of the Publish What You Pay (PWYP) Coalition in Madagascar.
Kevin Newe: Assistant Director - Illicit Finance Threat lead, His Majesty's Revenue and customs (HMRC), United Kingdom
Klaus Moosmayer:
Klaus Moosmayer was elected on May 22 2025 as member of the Supervisory Board of Deutsche Bank AG and serves on the Audit, Risk and Compensation Control Committees of the Board. Prior this appointment Klaus was until April 2025 the Chief Ethics, Risk and Compliance Officer and member of the Executive Committee of Novartis, a position he took over in December 2018. At Novartis, after closing out the legacy compliance matters of the corporation, he brought together ethics, policy governance, risk&crisis management and internal controls to an integrated assurance system which also included the responsible use of AI and new technologies. As a member of the Executive Committee he reported to the CEO and interacted closely with the Board of Directors including the Risk and Audit&Compliance Committee.

Before joining Novartis, Klaus spent 18 years in management positions of increasing responsibility at Siemens AG, serving as the company’s Chief Compliance Officer the last five years. Since 2006, he has been member of the core team tasked with addressing and resolving Siemens’ global corruption crisis.

He began his career after studying law and obtaining his doctor of jurisprudence at the university of Freiburg as an attorney and criminal defense lawyer.

Klaus Moosmayer has held Board and leadership positions at various international institutions. He led over many years the Anticorruption Committee of Business at OECD and subsequently served on its Executive Board. He was also Chair or Co-Chair of the B20 Integrity task forces during the G20 presidencies of Germany, Argentina, Saudi-Arabia, Indonesia and Italy. From 2021 until 2025 Klaus was Board member of SwissHoldings, the business association of Swiss based multinational companies.
Klaus publishes extensively in German, English and Spanish on ethics, risk management, compliance and governance and speaks frequently on these topics at national and international conferences. He was the first Chief Compliance Officer to speak in front of the General Assembly of the United Nations. In 2023, he was appointed to serve on the Council of the International Anti-Corruption Conference, which in collaboration with the government of the host country and the Secretariat of Transparency International organizes by-annually the world’s largest international gathering on integrity. In early 2025 he was appointed co-chair of the Global Future Council on Good Governance of the World Economic Forum for the term 2025-2026.
Kristen McGeeney: Kristen McGeeney is the Regional Director for MENA. She works with civil society and governments to improve the legal environment for civil society.
Kristen Sample: Kristen Sample is Coordinator of the Democracy Innovation Lab at the National Democratic Institute and the thematic lead for governance issues. She has more than 20 years of experience advancing democratic governance, anti-corruption, and inclusion and has published extensively on those themes. Previously, she served as head of the Andean Region and director of global programs at International IDEA, overseeing the organization’s comparative research.
Kristin Jean Rosella: Kristin Rosella is the Executive Director of LexCollective, a global coalition of lawyers and investigators working on interconnected human rights issues. She has almost 20 years of US and international litigation experience in financial crimes, forced labor, human trafficking, and atrocity crimes. She has represented trafficking survivors from Southeast Asia in cross-border civil and criminal cases seeking restitution, and she currently co-leads strategic litigation on behalf of affected communities against banking executives and financial institutions allegedly complicit in international crimes and money laundering. Previously, Kristin was a Senior Legal Consultant at the Khmer Rouge Tribunal in Cambodia and Program Director at Project Expedite Justice. She has trained over 1,000 civil society members, prosecutors, and law enforcement across Southeast Asia, East Africa, Latin America, and Eurasia.
Kumi Naidoo:
Kumi Naidoo is a human rights and climate justice activist from South Africa. He was Executive Director of Greenpeace International (from 2009 through 2015) and Secretary General of Amnesty International (from 2018 through 2019). Naidoo also served as the Secretary-General of CIVICUS, the international alliance for citizen participation, from 1998 to 2008.

He was an activist against the apartheid regime and its educational system in South Africa. Naidoo’s activism went from neighborhood organizing and community youth work to civil disobedience with mass mobilisations against the white controlled apartheid government. He has written about his activism in this period in his memoirs titled, “Letters to My Mother: The Making of a Troublemaker.
Laura Ferris:
Laura Ferris is an attorney and former US federal prosecutor for the United States Department of Justice. She is an expert on sanctions, terrorism financing, transnational criminal organizations, environmental crimes, and money laundering.

During her time as a prosecutor, Laura specialized on fraud, money laundering, violent crimes, and terrorism, serving three years as the Chief of the White-Collar Crime Unit. Laura led and worked with several criminal task forces, including the Joint Terrorism Task Force (JTTF), as well as Hi-tech Crimes and SARs (Suspicious Activity Reports) Review task forces.

From 2015-2022, Laura served with the US. Department of the Treasury as legal advisor to the Office of Foreign Assets Control on several sanctions programs and then as Assistant Chief Counsel, Enforcement and Liaison Divisions, for the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), the US financial intelligence unit.  At FinCEN she also served as Chief of Staff and Special Advisor to the Director.  In 2019 she established an overseas FinCEN position based out of the US Embassy in The Netherlands working at Europol as a liaison officer focused on increasing sharing of financial intelligence related to transnational criminal and national security threats. While overseas she also developed and led FinCEN’s first environmental crimes initiative, including outreach, information sharing, partnership meetings, and FinCEN’s first environmental crime publications, specifically an Environmental Crime Notice and a Financial Threat Analysis on Illegal Wildlife Trafficking.

Currently, Laura serves as the Director of Programs for the Sentry.
Laura Stefan: Stefan is the Executive Director of Expert Forum, an international anticorruption and justice expert and former Romania Justice Ministry director.
Le Thanh Forsberg: First Secretary / Senior Advisor - Research, HumanRights, Democracy & Rule of Law, Embassy of Sweden, Bangkok
Leilani Reklai: Editor/Publisher, Palau Island Times; vice chair Pacific Anti-Corruption Journalists Network
Leland Lazarus: Associate Director of National Security at Florida International University's Jack D. Gordon Institute of Public Policy; former U.S. Foreign Service Officer; former Special Assistant to two SOUTHCOM Commanders
Leslie Tsai: Over the last two decades, Leslie Tsai has built a global reputation as a strategic advocate and advisor to good governance efforts and champions around the world. A leading voice in the field, she has presented at TEDx, appeared on panels of international experts, and written articles on transparency and accountability published by the Financial Times, Chronicle of Philanthropy, World Bank blogs, and beyond. As the Director of Integrity Programs of the Chandler Foundation, she leads international efforts to support good governance, expand transparency and accountability, and develop robust international and national anti-corruption ecosystems. Prior to joining the Chandler Foundation in 2016, Leslie was on the executive team of Microclinic International, a global health nonprofit preventing deadly, chronic diseases in the U.S. and abroad. Early in her career, Leslie spent a year at the World Bank supporting financial sector development in Africa. She has worked at the African Development Bank, the Supreme Court of Rwanda, the Special Court for Sierra Leone. Leslie has been honored as a John Gardner Fellow at the World Bank, a term member of the Council on Foreign Relations, a World Economic Forum Global Shaper, and a Shafik Gabr U.S.- Egypt Exchange Fellow. She started her legal career at the law firm Sullivan & Cromwell. Leslie received her J.D. from Harvard Law School and her bachelor’s degree from the University of California, Berkeley.
Lesly Henderson-Rubio: Director for the Americas of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and lead of the Business Rule of Law Coalition
Lilian Ekeanyanwu: Lilian Ekeanyanwu is an attorney at law and retired as the head of the Technical Unit on Governance and Anti-Corruption Reforms - TUGAR, a government of Nigeria institution with mandate to provide coordinated data through empirical research and facilitate inter-agency coordination. She currently works as an anti-corruption consultant at the UNODC in Nigeria. Ms. Ekeanyanwu has done work in anti-corruption research and programming and as the Head of TUGAR, led the process of Corruption Risk Assessments in Nigeria. She coordinated the development of a country-specific methodology for conducting Corruption Risk Assessments which has been variously deployed. She has done training and research work on Global and regional anti-corruption Conventions and on Gender and Corruption. Ms. Ekeanyanwu is a member of the International Council of Transparency International and has coordinated and moderated workshops in several past IACC sessions especially on Gender and corruption. @Nwadinma
Linas Pernavas:
Mr Linas Pernavas from the 19th of June, 2023 is serving as a Director of the Special Investigation Service of the Republic of Lithuania.

In 1999 he graduated from the Lithuanian University of Law, in 2005 from Vilnius University and obtained a Master of Law qualification.

With a career spanning over two decades, Mr Pernavas joined the interior affairs system in 1995 and steadily climbed the ranks. His career began at the Ignalina District Police Headquarters.

In 2005-2008 he was the Chief of Zarasai District Police Headquarters, in 2008-2014 he served as a Chief of Utena County Police Headquarters and in 2014 he was a Chief of Kaunas District Police Headquarters.

Between 2014 and 2019 he was the Commissioner General of Lithuanian Police.

Mr. Pernavas launched the Police reform which increased public safety, increased the number of police officers on patrol and improved working conditions for officers. The reform made it possible to double the number of officers on the streets, to respond more quickly to the most dangerous calls, and to raise officers’ salaries. During his service as the Commissioner General of Lithuanian Police the public trust in police was on the rise and the highest.

Mr. Pernavas together with other heads of the Lithuanian Police established the Charity and Support Fund for Police Employees. The main and only purpose of the fund is to help officials and employees in extremely critical and difficult situations.

From 2019 (November) till 2023 (June) he served as Lithuania’s police attaché to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and remained there.

In May 2023 the Lithuanian Parliament approved Mr Pernavas as the director of the Special Investigation Service of the Republic of Lithuania. The agency’s main functions are the investigation of corruption cases, corruption prevention, and anti-corruption intelligence.

In 2023 he was elected as the President of the European Partners Against Corruption (EPAC) and the European Union Anti-Corruption Contact Network (EACN). EPAC/EACN is the largest and oldest European network of anti-corruption authorities and police oversight bodies. The aim of the EPAC/EACN network is to strengthen cooperation in the exchange of good practice in the fight against corruption and police oversight.

Mr Pernavas was awarded numerous times throughout his career: the Officer’s Cross of the Order of the Grand Duke Gediminasof Lithuania, the Medal of the Lithuanian Armed Forces “For Merit”, the 1st Degree Cross “100 for Estonian Police”, the 1st Degree Badge of Honour of the Dignitary Protection Service and many other.
Luciana Torchiaro: Luciana Torchiaro is Regional Advisor for Latin America and the Caribbean at Transparency International, where she leads and supports the organization’s regional work and network across Latin America and the Caribbean. She has worked with Transparency International for more than a decade and has contributed to initiatives addressing corruption, democracy, gender, and institutional accountability across the region. Previously, she worked at the Friedrich Ebert Foundation in Buenos Aires and as a technical advisor at the Secretariat of International Affairs of Tierra del Fuego, Argentina
Luis V. Villaherrera: Luis V. Villaherrera is a Salvadoran social entrepreneur, technology strategist, and Obama Foundation Fellow, the first from the region to receive the distinction. He is the Founder of TRACODA and NovaGen Forward, where he develops technology-driven solutions aimed at strengthening democratic institutions, improving transparency, and expanding economic opportunities across Latin America. His work sits at the intersection of technology, civic innovation, and entrepreneurship, bringing together governments, civil society organizations, and private sector partners to address complex social challenges through scalable, human-centered solutions.
Magistrada Yeni Berenice Reynoso: Prosecutor General of the Republic, Public Ministry of the Dominican Republic.
Maiwand Rahyab:
Maiwand Rahyab is the founder and C.E.O. of Resilient Societies, an emerging global initiative dedicated to protecting civic space and empowering democracy advocates and human rights defenders working under authoritarian regimes or in exile. Resilient Societies advances inclusive platforms such as the Resilience Network and the Ottawa Civic Space Summit, helping restore the voice, agency and relevance of civil society actors confronting repression and transnational threats.

Before relocating to Canada, he held senior leadership positions with the National Democratic Institute and Counterpart International, and served as the inaugural executive director of the Afghanistan Institute for Civil Society. His perspectives on civil society, democratic resilience and exile politics have appeared in the Ottawa Citizen, Montreal Gazette, The Diplomat and other media outlets.

Drawing on both lived experience and global expertise, he brings a compelling voice to urgent debates on civic space, democratic backsliding and the future of exile activism.
Mandeep Tiwana: A human rights lawyer by training, Mandeep specialises in legislation relating to the core civil society freedoms of expression, association and peaceful assembly. He is passionate about improving civil society’s participation in decision making, and has written extensively on the intersection  between civil society, sustainable development and international affairs. Previously, Mandeep advised the International Committee of the Red Cross in New Delhi. He has also worked with the Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative where he helped develop human rights modules for Commonwealth Parliamentarians and co-authored a citizens’ handbook on human rights commissions in India.  Presently Mandeep oversees CIVICUS’s work on defending civic freedoms and promoting democratic values while leading organisational engagement at the UN headquarters in New York.
Manuel Espinoza de los Monteros de la Pa:
Manuel has vast experience in advising both companies and public entities and has coordinated and supervised projects in over 70 countries. He co-founded LegalHelix and is a Senior Fellow at the Carol and Lawrence Zicklin Center for Business Ethics Research at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton Business School.

As a lawyer in Germany, he managed a network of boutique law firms from more than 30 jurisdictions specializing in white-collar crime and business integrity, and collaborated with law firms in different countries, including Spain and the US on corporate integrity projects. He also served as a consultant for international organisations, including the WTO and the UNODC and participated in a project of the European Commission on the harmonization of corporate criminal liability in Member States. He is a frequent speaker at international fora.
Marco Perez: Asesor en Cooperación con Sector Privado, GIZ México
Maria Isabel Torres: María Isabel Torres has been the Programme Director at Mongabay Latam, a leading environmental journalism news outlet, for the past ten years. Mongabay Latam relies on a network of over 100 journalists across Latin America, and its stories are frequently republished by the region's top media outlets. The organisation's investigations have received several prestigious journalistic awards, including the Rey de España Award, the Inter American Press Association Award and the Global Shining Light Award .Maria Isabel brings over twenty years of experience in print, television and digital media to her role, and holds a master’s degree in Visual Anthropology.
Maria Karienova: Maria has been working on community & network development for nonprofit. At the Center, she focuses to bridging journalism with strategic audience.
Maria McFarland Sánchez-Moreno: Maria McFarland Sánchez-Moreno is CEO of RepresentUs, the largest grassroots anti-corruption group in the United States. She is a Peruvian-American advocate, author, and lawyer with two decades of global experience on issues of corruption, authoritarianism, organized crime, and human rights. Maria has held multiple senior positions at Human Rights Watch and served as executive director of the Drug Policy Alliance. Her narrative non-fiction book, “There Are No Dead Here: A Story of Murder and Denial in Colombia,” won the 2018 Juan E. Méndez Human Rights Book Award.
Maria Rosa Darrigo: Researcher and policy specialist in ecology and sustainable development, bridging science, policy, and advocacy across Latin America
Martin Hoppe: Martin Hoppe is Head of Division Governance at the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
Martin Vladimirov: Director, Program "Geoeconimics", Center for the Study of Democracy (CSD)
María de la Luz Mijangos Borja: Federal Prosecutor, Titular de la Fiscalía Especializada en materia de Combate a la Corrupción (FEMCC), Mexico
María de los Ángeles Estrada González: María de los Ángeles is a Mexican lawyer and international affairs specialist with extensive experience in transparency, anti-corruption, open government, whistleblower protection, and public-sector integrity. She is the founder and director of Mexico’s Transparency, Anti-Corruption, and Digitalization Initiative, where she leads research and projects aimed at strengthening integrity, accountability, and institutional capacity. She also advises the National Whistleblower Center in Washington, D.C., on corruption reporting, whistleblower protections, and citizen participation.
Matthew Murray: Expert in national security, energy, governance, rule of law and anti-corruption, with more than 40 years of experience across government institutions, multi-national corporations, multilateral organizations, civil society, and academia. Mr. Murray served as Deputy Assistant Secretary for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at the U.S. Department of Commerce (2012–2015), Senior Governance and Rule of Law Advisor at USAID (2016-2017), and International Commissioner of the Independent Joint Anti- Corruption Monitoring and Evaluation Committee in Afghanistan (2017-2019). He has over 15 years of experience working with Ukraine government, business, and civil society leaders to build institutions, laws, and practices to prevent corruption and facilitate economic security and prosperity. Mr. Murray chaired the commission responsible for selecting the Head of the National Agency on Corruption Prevention of Ukraine (NACP) (2023-2024. He is an Adjunct Professor at Georgetown University and Columbia University.
Matthew Stephenson: Matthew Stephenson is Professor of Law at Harvard Law School, where he teaches administrative law, legislation and regulation, anti-corruption law, and political economy of public law. His research focuses on the application of positive political theory to public law, particularly in the areas of administrative procedure, anti-corruption, judicial institutions, and separation of powers. Prior to joining the Harvard Law School faculty, Professor Stephenson clerked for Senior Judge Stephen Williams on the D.C. Circuit and for Justice Anthony Kennedy on the Supreme Court. He received his J.D. and Ph.D. (political science) from Harvard in 2003, and his B.A. from Harvard College in 1997.
Maíra Martini:
Maíra Martini has been with the Transparency International Secretariat since 2011. Most recently, she served as Head of Policy & Advocacy, where her leadership was pivotal in shaping the organisation’s strategic direction. She has led Transparency International on efforts in antimoney laundering, beneficial ownership transparency and combating illicit financial flows. Martini is a lawyer with a Master’s degree in Public Policy from the Hertie School of Governance in Berlin.

Beyond her work at Transparency International, Martini has authored numerous reports and analyses on antcorruption and good governance and served on the steering groups of OpenOwnership, and the Anti-Corruption Data Collective. Her achievements were recognised in 2022 when she received the Transparency International’s Amalia Award for Professional Excellence.
Mbali Baduza: Mbali Baduza is CEO of WeThePeopleSA, which promotes knowledge and understanding of South Africa's Constitution, its making and its impact on society.
Mercedes de Freitas:
Mercedes is Founder and Executive Director of Transparencia Venezuela, and a member of the Board of Directors of Transparency International from 2014 to 2017. She has directed Cívitas Venezuela since 2005. In 2016 she founded and directed Vendata. In 2006 she co-founded Crea Resultados. In 2017 she launched and led CampusTransparencia.com, an online training platform on transparency, justice, integrity, and anti-corruption; and in 2019, Espaja.com, a news and discourse verification platform, and the national Anti-Corruption Coalition movement. She co-founded and directed Becrack in 2020. She is a member of the coordinating team of Quiero Elegir.

Since 2020 she has served on the board of the Venezuela Corruption Taskforce. Since 2023 she has been a member of the Board of Directors of the Latin American and Caribbean Network for Democracy (REDLAD). She was invited as a civil-society speaker to the United Nations Security Council in special sessions on Venezuela in September 2018 and January 2026.

Since 2000 she has been a Fellow of Ashoka, the global network of social entrepreneurs, and in 2006 she won Ashoka's Champion ChangeMakers award. In 2019 she received the Anti-Corruption Leader Annual Award from the Americas Society/Council of the Americas. She was a member of ChangeMakers United in 2021. In 2024 she received Transparency International's Amalia Award for Individual Professional Excellence.

She has led more than 70 investigations into corruption networks, money laundering, and organized crime in Venezuela; has designed and directed dozens of events; and has been invited as a speaker and panelist at dozens of international events across dozens of countries.
Micol Martini: Micol Martini is a Senior Expert with over 20 years of experience working on issues related to governance, conflict, and insecurity.
Mitzi Jonelle Tan: Mitzi Jonelle Tan is a full-time climate justice activist based in Metro Manila, Philippines. She is an organizer with Fridays For Future International and FFF MAPA (Most Affected Peoples and Areas) making sure that voices from the Global South are heard, amplified, and given space. She is also part of the steering committee of the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty and the Youth Climate Justice Fund. A strong voice on anti-imperialism, anti-colonization, and the intersectionality of the climate crisis, she is committed to changing the system and building a world that prioritizes people and planet, not profit, through collective action, system change, love and joy.
Mohammed Benalilou: President, L'Instance nationale de la probité, de la prévention et de la lutte contre la corruption (INPPLC)
Naomi Roht-Arriaza: Co-Chair of the Victims of Corruption Working Group of the Global Civil Society Coalition for the UNCAC and author of Fighting Grand Corruption: Transnational and Human Rights Approaches in Latin America and Beyond
Nicola Allocca:
Nicola Allocca is an international executive, lecturer, and thought leader in governance, risk management, compliance, and anti-corruption, with a strong focus on the integration of artificial intelligence into business decision-making.

He currently serves as Chair of the Business at OECD (BIAC) Integrity & Anti-Corruption Committee, where he leads global initiatives to promote transparency, ethical business conduct, and resilient governance systems. He has also played a key role in international policy dialogues, including the B20, contributing to the advancement of integrity frameworks in complex and rapidly evolving environments.

With cross-industry experience spanning infrastructure, aerospace, steel, consulting, and retail, Nicola has held senior leadership roles where he has driven the transformation of compliance from a control function into a strategic enabler of performance and value creation.

He also serves as a Short-Term Expert for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI), contributing to international capacity-building projects focused on governance, legality, and institutional strengthening.

Alongside his executive career, he teaches Responsible Business Conduct at the University of Rome Tor Vergata and contributes to international master programs focused on public procurement and anti-corruption.

His work sits at the intersection of governance and innovation, advocating for a model where there is no trade-off between performance and compliance, and where AI is recognized as a new stakeholder in organizational ecosystem
Nicolás Crow:
Nicolas Crow is an Ecuadorian lawyer, Ambassador of the International Organization of Youth, and Founder and Executive Director of the YAC Foundation, one of the largest youth-led anti-corruption organizations in the Americas. The foundation focuses on governance, transparency, and combating public corruption to advance sustainable development. Having grown up in Ecuador and witnessed the country’s transformation from being considered one of the safest nations in Latin America to facing an unprecedented security crisis, Nicolas developed a strong interest in understanding how public corruption and institutional weaknesses directly impact people’s lives, opportunities, and development prospects, particularly for young people.

Alongside his work at the YAC Foundation, Nicolas operates at the intersection of international law, public policy, public and regulatory affairs, and emerging technologies. He is committed to fostering collaboration among stakeholders to address emerging challenges and deliver tangible development outcomes, while advocating for stronger anti-corruption efforts and greater youth participation in national and international decision-making processes. Nicolas holds a law degree from Universidad San Francisco de Quito and has pursued further studies at the University of Cambridge, Peking University, and Beijing International Studies University, including coursework in development economics and Mandarin Chinese.
Nina Jankowicz: Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, American Sunlight Project.
